abstracts.abstract: The separation between quantum and classical computational power remains one of the central open problems in quantum complexity theory. This paper introduces a novel framework for analyzing the relative power of quantum circuits with restricted depth and classical communication protocols, establishing unconditional separations that do not rely on any complexity-theoretic assumptions. Our approach leverages a refined notion of quantum steering in multi-prover interactive proof systems, demonstrating that a new class of efficiently preparable quantum states exhibits statistical properties that cannot be replicated by polynomial-size classical circuits with bounded parallel time. We introduce the concept of quantum coherence depth as a complexity measure and prove that logarithmic separation in this measure yields provable advantage for distributed quantum computing tasks. The technical contribution involves constructing an explicit sampling problem that lies in constant-depth quantum circuits but outside the capability of any classical parallel computation of polylogarithmic depth. This work fundamentally reshapes our understanding of where quantum advantages emerge, shifting focus from computational complexity assumptions to unconditional proofs. The results have direct implications for quantum cryptography and the design of quantum network protocols where physical assumptions about communication constraints are minimal.

Quantum amplitude estimation represents a fundamental subroutine in quantum machine learning and optimization, yet existing algorithms exhibit query complexity that scales as O(1/ε) for achieving precision ε. This work presents a refined analysis of the quantum amplitude estimation framework that achieves quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo methods with significantly improved constant factors. We develop a novel constructive approach to quantum phase estimation that reduces the number of controlled operations required by a factor of log(1/ε) while maintaining the asymptotic optimality in query complexity. Our algorithm introduces a family of optimal measurement bases derived from discrete prolate spheroidal wave functions, which adaptively concentrate measurement resources on the relevant spectral features. Theoretical analysis proves that our method achieves query complexity O(1/(ε·log(1/ε))) with high probability, improving upon the best previously known bound by a factor of log(1/ε) in the practical regime where ε is not exponentially small. We further demonstrate applications to quantum portfolio optimization and quantum integration, showing concrete advantages in realistic financial modeling scenarios. The analysis includes rigorous error bounds and provides guidance for practical implementation on near-term quantum devices with finite coherence times.

Current quantum programming languages lack native support for variational quantum algorithms that require tight integration between classical optimization loops and quantum circuit execution. This paper introduces Questo, a novel quantum programming language designed from first principles to support hybrid classical-quantum computation with formal verification capabilities. Questo adopts a linear typing discipline that naturally captures the no-cloning principle while providing dependent types for specifying and verifying quantum circuit properties at compile time. The language introduces quantum effect handlers that abstract over different quantum backend architectures, enabling portable programs that can execute on both real quantum hardware and simulators without modification. We present a type-safe intermediate representation that supports quantum circuit optimizations including gate fusion, commutation analysis, and hardware-native decomposition. The compiler employs a static scheduling analysis that minimizes quantum coherence time requirements by reordering circuit operations based on qubit connectivity and classical feedforward requirements. Our implementation includes a certified optimizer using the Coq proof assistant that provides end-to-end correctness guarantees. Benchmark results demonstrate that Questo programs achieve comparable performance to hand-optimized quantum circuits while providing strong correctness guarantees that are impossible to express in existing quantum programming frameworks.

Quantum error correction codes require syndrome extraction circuits that consume significant hardware resources and introduce substantial latency in fault-tolerant quantum computation. This paper presents an automated framework for synthesizing optimized syndrome extraction circuits that reduces overhead by exploiting code-specific symmetries and hardware-native gate sets. Our approach formulates circuit synthesis as a constraint satisfaction problem that explicitly models the restricted connectivity of trapped-ion quantum hardware and the specific two-qubit gate decompositions available on this platform. We introduce a novel heuristic search algorithm that explores the space of equivalent syndrome extraction sequences using a cost function that accounts for both circuit depth and qubit movement overhead. For the surface code under various distance parameters, our synthesized circuits achieve an average reduction of 23% in two-qubit gate count and 31% reduction in average syndrome extraction latency compared to state-of-the-art手工设计的电路。We provide experimental validation on a 11-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor, demonstrating that the optimized circuits maintain logical error rates consistent with theoretical predictions while enabling faster operation. The synthesis framework is fully automated and integrates with existing quantum software stacks, making optimized syndrome extraction accessible without expert knowledge of error correction implementation details.
